description.en: None of the goals of the conversation is reached, or the learner talks about something else.
One goal is touched with a word or two. Most goals are missed.
Some goals are reached, but at least one important goal is missed.
All the goals of the conversation are reached, in short simple sentences.
All the goals are reached, and the learner adds one useful detail of their own.
No usable English words.
Single words or memorised chunks only, repeated again and again.
A small set of familiar words and phrases, with a lot of repeating.
Enough familiar words and phrases for the conversation without much repeating.
Familiar words and phrases used with some variety, and one or two words beyond the unit's own list.
So many mistakes that the meaning is lost.
Many mistakes, including in the basic patterns of the unit. The meaning is often unclear.
Mistakes in the unit's basic patterns in about half of the sentences. The meaning can still be followed.
The unit's basic patterns are mostly right. A few mistakes do not hide the meaning.
The unit's basic patterns are right almost every time.
Nothing is connected. No reply follows from the one before it.
Separate words or phrases with no link to what was just said.
Short replies that follow the conversation in a loose way.
Short replies that fit what was just said, in a sensible order.
Replies that fit what was just said and link to earlier turns with simple words such as and, but or because.
The learner does not reply to the other speaker.
Replies with a word or two, often not to the question that was asked.
Answers simple questions but rarely asks one or keeps the exchange going.
Answers simple questions and asks at least one question of their own.
Keeps the exchange going: answers, asks, and reacts to what the other speaker says.
